cards.details: Vasco da Gama departs from Lisbon with four ships (São Gabriel, São Rafael, Bérrio, and a storage ship) sponsored by King Manuel I of Portugal.
Guided by Arab navigator Ibn Majid from Malindi, Gama lands at Kappad near Calicut (Kozhikode). Received by Hindu ruler Zamorin. Departs in August with spice cargo worth 60x the voyage cost.
Gama returns with a heavily armed fleet of 20 ships. Demands the Zamorin expel all Muslim merchants. Establishes the first Portuguese factory (trading post) at Cochin.
Appointed as Viceroy of India to curb corruption among Portuguese officials. Arrives in Cochin, where he contracts malaria and dies in December 1524.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Trap 1: The Pilot's Identity: UPSC often tests the identity of the pilot who guided Gama to Calicut. It was **Ibn Majid**, a prominent Gujarati/Arab navigator, NOT a Portuguese sailor.

Trap 2: The Viceroy Status: Vasco da Gama was NOT the first Viceroy of India; that title belongs to **Francisco de Almeida** (1505). Gama only became Viceroy much later, during his third voyage in 1524.

Trap 3: The First Factory: The first Portuguese factory in India was established at **Cochin** (1503), not Calicut. Gama's first voyage only secured trade agreements, but actual factory construction began during his second voyage.

sections.title: 1. The First Voyage (1497-1499): Bypassing Middlemen
sections.content:
Vasco da Gama's first voyage laid the foundation of direct Euro-Asian maritime trade:

Route & Discoveries
  • Lisbon Departure: Departed July 1497, rounded the Cape of Good Hope, and sailed up the East African coast.
  • Ibn Majid's Help: At Malindi (Kenya), Gama hired Gujarati/Arab pilot Ibn Majid, who knew the monsoon wind patterns of the Indian Ocean.
  • Landing: Landed at Calicut in May 1498. The spice cargo he brought back sold for 60 times the cost of the trip.

masteryZone.q: Which ship served as Vasco da Gama's flagship during his historic first voyage to India in 1497-1499 CE?
masteryZone.sol: The São Gabriel was the flagship, commanded by Vasco da Gama himself. His brother Paulo commanded the São Rafael.

masteryZone.q: Who was the legendary pilot who guided Vasco da Gama's fleet from Malindi across the Arabian Sea to Calicut?
masteryZone.sol: Ahmad Ibn Mājid (often identified as a Gujarati or Arab navigator) guided the fleet using his expertise of monsoon winds.

masteryZone.q: Which Portuguese monarch sponsored and commissioned Vasco da Gama's first voyage to find a direct sea route to India?
masteryZone.sol: King Manuel I ('The Fortunate') sponsored the voyage. King John II had made initial plans but died before execution.

masteryZone.q: Where exactly did Vasco da Gama first set foot on Indian soil in May 1498 CE?
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama landed at Kappad beach, located about 15 km north of Calicut (Kozhikode).

masteryZone.q: What major disaster befell Vasco da Gama's fleet on the return journey from India to Portugal?
opts: Destruction of São Rafael due to crew loss from scurvy
Total loss of spice cargo in a storm near Madagascar
Capture of the flagship by Arab pirates off Mombasa
masteryZone.sol: Scurvy decimated the crew on the return leg, forcing Gama to burn the São Rafael near East Africa due to a lack of sailors.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following ships were part of Vasco da Gama's original four-vessel fleet that left Lisbon in 1497? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The fleet comprised São Gabriel (flagship), São Rafael, Bérrio, and an unnamed storage ship.

masteryZone.q: Which East African coastal settlements did Vasco da Gama visit before crossing the Indian Ocean? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama visited Mozambique, Mombasa (where he faced hostility), and Malindi (where he was warmly received).

masteryZone.q: What were the main commercial objectives of Vasco da Gama's first expedition? (Select all that apply)
opts: Securing direct access to the spice trade
Establishing direct royal diplomacy in India
masteryZone.sol: The first voyage sought trade and routes, not territorial conquests, which occurred later under Albuquerque.

masteryZone.q: Which factors contributed to the high mortality rate among the crew of the first voyage? (Select all that apply)
opts: Outbreak of scurvy during the long crossings
Lack of fresh water and proper provisions
Hostile skirmishes along the East African coast
Malaria outbreak in the Cape Verde islands
masteryZone.sol: Scurvy, dietary deficiency, and hostile clashes killed nearly half of the original 170 crew members.

masteryZone.q: Identify the cargo Vasco da Gama successfully brought back to Lisbon in 1499. (Select all that apply)
opts: Heavy quantities of Indian cotton textiles
masteryZone.sol: He brought back spices (pepper, cinnamon, cloves, ginger) and fine Asian goods like porcelain and gems.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Ahmad Ibn Mājid was a Portuguese officer who plotted the route using advanced European charts.
masteryZone.sol: He was a local Indian Ocean pilot (Gujarati/Arab) who possessed traditional navigation knowledge.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama was named Viceroy of India immediately upon his return in 1499.
masteryZone.sol: He was given titles like 'Admiral of the Seas of Arabia' but only became Viceroy in 1524.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The first voyage sailed through the Mediterranean Sea and Suez Canal to reach India.
masteryZone.sol: The Suez Canal did not exist; they sailed around the Cape of Good Hope.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The spice cargo returned by Gama was sold for roughly 60 times the cost of the entire expedition.
masteryZone.sol: Despite losing two ships and half the crew, the spice cargo proved immensely profitable.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The São Rafael flagship returned safely to Lisbon port.
masteryZone.sol: São Rafael was burned because there were not enough surviving crew members to sail it.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The entire outbound and inbound journey took less than 12 months to complete.
masteryZone.sol: It took more than two years, departing in July 1497 and returning in August 1499.

masteryZone.q: True or False: King Manuel I was known as 'The Fortunate' due to the wealth brought by the direct route.
masteryZone.sol: The opening of the route brought tremendous wealth and prestige to his reign.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama was killed by the Zamorin's forces during his first voyage.
masteryZone.sol: He returned safely to Lisbon and died decades later in Cochin during his third voyage.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Vasco da Gama's fleet:
1. It consisted of three standard caravels and one supply ship.
2. The São Rafael was the largest ship and served as the flagship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: São Gabriel was the flagship. The ships were square-rigged naus, not standard caravels.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the navigation of the first voyage:
1. Vasco da Gama used astronomical navigation using the astrolabe.
2. The fleet used Arabic navigational charts purchased in Lisbon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: They used astrolabes and solar declination tables. Arabic charts were only obtained later in East Africa.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the return journey of the first voyage, consider these statements:
1. The crossing of the Arabian Sea took three months due to lack of wind.
2. Nicolau Coelho's ship Bérrio arrived back in Portugal before Vasco da Gama's flagship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The crossing took 3 months (vs 23 days outbound) due to calm winds, causing severe scurvy. Bérrio arrived in July 1499, while Gama delayed at Azores.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding pilot Ibn Majid:
1. He was a native of Malindi who wanted to migrate to India.
2. He possessed precise knowledge of the seasonal monsoon wind changes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: He was a Gujarati/Arab pilot hired in Malindi who knew the monsoon winds of the Indian Ocean.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the commercial impact of the first voyage, consider these statements:
1. Spices brought back were sold at the Lisbon spice market (Casa da India).
2. Venice immediately declared war on Portugal to protect its trade route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The spices were sold through Casa da Índia. Venice did not declare war immediately, though they suffered commercial decline.

masteryZone.q: Why did Vasco da Gama perform a wide westward arc in the Atlantic Ocean during the outbound journey?
masteryZone.sol: He executed the 'Volta do mar' maneuver to catch the prevailing westerly winds, thereby bypassing the adverse currents and doldrums of the Gulf of Guinea.

masteryZone.q: Why was the return crossing of the Arabian Sea so catastrophic compared to the outward journey?
masteryZone.sol: Gama sailed against the summer monsoon winds in August. Lacking favorable winds, the crossing took 3 months, leading to extreme scurvy and starvation.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Sultan of Malindi welcome Vasco da Gama while Mozambique and Mombasa expelled him?
masteryZone.sol: Malindi was in a regional rivalry with Mombasa and saw the well-armed Portuguese as potential allies to balance local power.

masteryZone.q: How did the discovery of the Cape Route affect the prices of spices in Western Europe?
masteryZone.sol: It bypassed the heavy taxation imposed by Ottoman, Mamluk, and Venetian middlemen, eventually lowering wholesale spice costs while concentrating trade wealth in Lisbon.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama's crew navigate without sight of land during the Atlantic crossing?
masteryZone.sol: They used celestial navigation, measuring the altitude of the sun and stars (like the Pole Star) using brass astrolabes and quadrant instruments.

masteryZone.q: How did the loss of crew members affect the fleet's composition on the return voyage?
masteryZone.sol: With around half the crew dead, Gama was forced to abandon and burn the São Rafael near Mombasa, distributing the survivors onto the São Gabriel and Bérrio.

masteryZone.q: Examine the role of Malindi as a strategic junction in the Portuguese maritime network.
masteryZone.sol: Malindi served as a safe haven providing fresh water, provisions, and pilots. This alliance remained a cornerstone of Portuguese navigation along the Swahili coast for decades.

masteryZone.q: Analyze the impact of scurvy on the viability of early long-distance Portuguese voyages.
masteryZone.sol: Scurvy caused massive crew loss (often 50%+). It highlights the physiological limits of early modern exploration before the connection between fresh citrus fruits and preventing the disease was established.

masteryZone.q: Discuss the significance of the return of the ship Bérrio under Nicolau Coelho.
masteryZone.sol: Bérrio was a caravel and the fastest ship. It separated from the flagship and arrived first in Lisbon, delivering the first proof that the route to India was open.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Volta do Mar' (Turn of the Sea) to a student.
masteryZone.sol: It is a sailing technique where navigators sail in a wide circle to find favorable winds rather than sailing directly against head-winds. Gama sailed far west near Brazil to round Africa successfully.

masteryZone.q: Describe how monsoon wind patterns dictated trade schedules in the Indian Ocean.
masteryZone.sol: Winds blow from the southwest in summer (May-Sept) aiding travel to India, and from the northeast in winter (Oct-April) aiding return voyages. Sailing against these caused long delays.

masteryZone.q: Explain the structure and command hierarchy of Vasco da Gama's first fleet.
masteryZone.sol: The fleet was state-commissioned, combining heavy naus (ships) with a fast caravel (Bérrio) and a supply ship, commanded by Gama as captain-major, with experienced pilots.

sections.title: 2. Encounters with Zamorin of Calicut
sections.content:
The interactions between Gama and the Calicut ruler (Zamorin) shaped early European diplomacy in India:

Diplomatic Tensions
  • Commercial Rivalry: Arab merchants already dominated Calicut's trade and opposed Portuguese presence.
  • Zamorin's Reaction: The Zamorin welcomed Gama but was unimpressed by the cheap European gifts (cloth, hats, coral) presented. He refused to grant exclusive trading monopolies.

masteryZone.q: What was the hereditary title held by the Hindu ruler of Calicut who received Vasco da Gama in 1498 CE?
masteryZone.sol: The ruler of Calicut held the title Zamorin, a Portuguese corruption of the Malayalam word 'Samudiri' meaning Lord of the Sea.

masteryZone.q: How did the Zamorin of Calicut react to the gifts presented by Vasco da Gama during their first audience?
opts: He was disappointed and unimpressed by their low quality
He immediately accepted them as high tribute
He imprisoned Gama for insulting the crown
He traded them for gold coins
masteryZone.sol: The gifts (hats, cloth, sugar, honey) were cheap merchant items. The Zamorin and his court ridiculed them as unfit for a king.

masteryZone.q: Which faction of merchants in Calicut strongly opposed Vasco da Gama and tried to sabotage his trade negotiations?
masteryZone.sol: Arab merchants held a monopoly on spice exports in Calicut and rightly feared Portuguese naval armed competition.

masteryZone.q: What did the Zamorin demand from Vasco da Gama before allowing him to depart Calicut with his cargo?
opts: Payment of port customs duties in gold/silver
Surrender of the flagship São Gabriel
Conversion of the Portuguese crew to Hinduism
An alliance against the ruler of Cochin
masteryZone.sol: The Zamorin demanded standard port customs duties. Gama refused, claiming exemption as an ambassador, leading to a standoff.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama retaliate when the Zamorin temporarily detained some Portuguese factors and goods?
opts: He seized local hostages and sailed away with them
He launched a full naval invasion of Calicut city
He paid the custom duties double in value
He burned down the local temple
masteryZone.sol: To force the release of his men and goods, Gama captured several Calicut citizens and took them back to Lisbon.

masteryZone.q: Why were the Arab merchants of Calicut hostile towards the arrival of Vasco da Gama? (Select all that apply)
opts: They feared losing their lucrative monopoly on spice exports
They wanted to protect their religious influence at court
They realized the Portuguese intended to enforce a monopoly by naval force
They were allied with the British East India Company
masteryZone.sol: The Arab traders recognized that Portuguese armed ships aimed to seize the Indian Ocean trade by force and exclude other merchants.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following items did Vasco da Gama present to the Zamorin that were rejected as tribute? (Select all that apply)
opts: Fine gold coins and silver plates
masteryZone.sol: The gifts were simple trade goods of low value, lacking the gold, silver, or fine gems expected by an Indian king.

masteryZone.q: Which factors made Calicut a major trading hub on the Malabar Coast? (Select all that apply)
opts: Strategic location midway along the Indian Ocean trade network
Abundant local cultivation of high-quality black pepper
Open port policy welcoming merchants of all nationalities
Heavy Portuguese naval protection since the 14th century
masteryZone.sol: Calicut grew wealthy due to its location, pepper production, and tolerant commercial policy, long before Europeans arrived.

masteryZone.q: What were the main grievances of the Zamorin against Vasco da Gama during the first visit? (Select all that apply)
opts: The insultingly cheap gifts presented to the throne
Gama's refusal to pay standard port customs duties
The hostile abduction of Calicut citizens
The establishment of a fort without permission
masteryZone.sol: The Zamorin was offended by the poor gifts, the tax evasion, and the hostage-taking. No fort was established in 1498.

masteryZone.q: Identify the languages used to translate communications between Vasco da Gama and the Zamorin. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Portuguese was translated to Arabic (by bilingual convicts or merchants), which was then translated to Malayalam for the Zamorin.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Zamorin of Calicut was a Muslim Sultan belonging to the Adil Shahi dynasty.
masteryZone.sol: The Zamorin was a Hindu monarch belonging to the Nair/Samantaclan.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Zamorin granted Vasco da Gama a written treaty giving Portugal a monopoly on spice exports.
masteryZone.sol: He refused, stating Calicut was a free port open to all traders.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Arab merchants successfully persuaded the Zamorin to execute Vasco da Gama on his first visit.
masteryZone.sol: They urged execution or arrest, but the Zamorin only demanded taxes and let him leave after cargo exchanges.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama's gifts included fine European mechanical clocks that fascinated the court.
masteryZone.sol: No, his gifts were rudimentary items like brass basins and oil jars, which were laughed at.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Calicut was valued as a transit center where spices from Southeast Asia were transshipped.
masteryZone.sol: It was an entropic port where spices from Malacca were traded alongside local Malabar pepper.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama departed Calicut with a cargo of spices that he obtained without paying any duties.
masteryZone.sol: He loaded spices but left behind some factors and seized hostages in lieu of confiscated Portuguese goods.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The title Samudiri literally translates to 'Lord of the Sea'.
masteryZone.sol: Samudiri Raja means the king who rules the sea, emphasizing Calicut's maritime dependence.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Calicut was heavily fortified by the Portuguese during Vasco da Gama's first visit in 1498.
masteryZone.sol: No fortification took place during the first visit. Tensions were too high.

opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Communication was convoluted, going through multiple translations (Portuguese to Arabic, and then to Malayalam).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Arab merchants viewed the Portuguese arrival as a threat to their survival.
Reason: The Portuguese did not intend to trade peacefully but to use armed naval power to monopolize routes.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese policy of armed mercantilism was designed to forcefully destroy competitor trade.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Zamorin's court treated Gama with absolute royal honor.
Reason: They expected the Portuguese to bring massive treasures of European gold.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The initial reception was respectful, but the court soon mocked the cheap gifts, leading to a loss of prestige for Gama.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Calicut was a major transit point for Chinese silk and porcelain.
Reason: Calicut lay at the convergence of Chinese shipping routes and Western Indian Ocean routes.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Calicut's geographical location made it a major global transshipment hub.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama paid the customs duties demanded by the Zamorin.
Reason: The Portuguese crown had instructed Gama to strictly follow all local tax laws to secure long-term treaties.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Gama refused to pay the duties, claiming he was an ambassador and not a merchant, which caused the tax dispute.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The relationship between the Zamorin and the Portuguese remained hostile after 1499.
Reason: The Portuguese returned on subsequent voyages with heavy naval armaments to punish Calicut.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The mutual distrust of the first voyage escalated into open war in subsequent years.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Zamorin's administration:
1. The port officer (Shahbandar) of Calicut was traditionally an Arab merchant.
2. The administration relied heavily on customs duties (export taxes) on spices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Arab merchants held key administrative posts related to trade, and customs duties were the crown's primary revenue.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the gifts presented by Gama, consider these statements:
1. The gifts were chosen by the King of Portugal, who underestimated Indian royal wealth.
2. The Zamorin suggested that Gama should have brought gold or silver instead of washbasins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. The cheap items were standard for West African trade but insulted the wealthy Zamorin.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Calicut was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
2. The Zamorin was subordinate to the Bahmani Sultan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Calicut was an independent kingdom ruled by the Zamorin. It was not part of Vijayanagara or Bahmani empires.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the Arab merchants at Calicut, consider these statements:
1. They were led by a wealthy merchant family known as the Koya family.
2. They controlled the shipping vessels but did not interfere with local politics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The Koyas and Shabhandars exercised huge political influence over the Zamorin to protect their trade interests.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the hostages taken by Vasco da Gama:
1. The hostages were members of the Zamorin's own family.
2. They were taken to Lisbon and presented to the King of Portugal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The hostages were local merchants and fishermen, not the Zamorin's family. They were taken to Lisbon as proof of the voyage.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Zamorin refuse to give the Portuguese exclusive trading rights?
masteryZone.sol: The Zamorin followed a free-port policy. Granting a monopoly to Portugal would alienate Arab merchants and destroy Calicut's commercial foundation.

masteryZone.q: Why were the gifts Vasco da Gama brought considered an insult to the Zamorin?
masteryZone.sol: They consisted of cheap items (cloth, hats, honey) suited for primitive African trade, whereas Indian rulers were accustomed to receiving precious metals, gems, and fine goods.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Arab merchants have so much influence over the Calicut administration?
masteryZone.sol: They generated the vast majority of Calicut's tax revenue through shipping, and held key administrative posts like Shahbandar (port officer).

masteryZone.q: How did the linguistic barrier affect the initial meetings between Gama and the Zamorin?
masteryZone.sol: It created deep mistrust. Since no Portuguese spoke Malayalam and no local spoke Portuguese, messages went through multiple translations, leading to misinterpretations.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama use hostage-taking as a tool of coercion during his first visit?
masteryZone.sol: Gama kidnapped local citizens to leverage the release of Portuguese factors and goods detained by the Zamorin over unpaid taxes, establishing a precedent of force.

masteryZone.q: How did the trade rivalry at Calicut shape the future alliances of the Portuguese on the Malabar Coast?
masteryZone.sol: The hostility of Calicut forced the Portuguese to seek alliances with Calicut's rivals, notably the ruler of Cochin, which became the main Portuguese base.

masteryZone.q: Analyze the administrative role of Arab merchants in the port city of Calicut.
masteryZone.sol: Arab traders acted as financial backers, tax collectors, and diplomats for the Zamorin, integrating trade directly with the political structure.

masteryZone.q: Examine the gift-giving ritual in Indian courts as a study of cross-cultural diplomatic failure.
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese failure to provide appropriate prestige gifts showed a lack of diplomatic preparation, ruining their credibility in the eyes of the Zamorin.

masteryZone.q: Evaluate the Zamorin's policy of maintaining Calicut as a free-trade zone.
masteryZone.sol: The Zamorin allowed all merchants (Arabs, Gujaratis, Chinese) to trade on equal terms, which ensured high cargo volumes and port duties.

masteryZone.q: Explain the origin and meaning of the title 'Zamorin' to a student.
masteryZone.sol: It comes from the Malayalam 'Samudiri Raja', meaning 'Lord of the Sea', which highlights the maritime nature of his authority.

masteryZone.q: Describe the mechanisms of custom duty collection at Calicut port.
masteryZone.sol: Goods were inspected by the port officers, and taxes were levied based on cargo volume and value, typically paid in gold or silver coins.

masteryZone.q: Explain how the Portuguese threat altered the traditional trade rules in the Indian Ocean.
masteryZone.sol: Before 1498, trade was largely unarmed and open. The Portuguese introduced armed ships and the Cartaz system, forcing merchants to buy protection.

sections.title: 3. The Second Voyage (1502): Gunboat Diplomacy
sections.content:
Vasco da Gama returned in 1502 with a militarized mission to establish Portuguese dominance by force:

Armed Aggression
  • Fleet of 20 Ships: Armed with heavy cannons, Gama aimed to enforce the crown monopoly.
  • Demands & Blockade: Demanded the Zamorin expel all Muslim merchants. When the Zamorin refused, Gama bombarded Calicut and captured merchant ships.
  • Cochin Factory: Established the first trading post at Cochin (Kochi), forming an alliance with Cochin's ruler (a rival of the Zamorin).

masteryZone.q: In which year did Vasco da Gama return to India for his highly militarized second voyage?
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama returned in 1502 CE with a fleet of 20 heavily armed ships to establish dominance.

masteryZone.q: Which explorer commanded the intermediate Portuguese expedition to India (1500 CE) between Gama's first and second voyages?
masteryZone.sol: Pedro Álvares Cabral commanded the second Portuguese expedition in 1500, discovering Brazil along the way.

masteryZone.q: With which regional rival of the Zamorin did Vasco da Gama establish a crucial alliance during his second voyage?
masteryZone.sol: Gama allied with the Raja of Cochin, who welcomed the Portuguese to counter Calicut's hegemony.

masteryZone.q: What violent act did Vasco da Gama commit against Calicut during his second voyage in 1502 CE?
opts: He bombarded the city and destroyed Calicut's merchant fleet
He captured and occupied the Zamorin's palace
He executed the Zamorin during negotiations
He poisoned the city's water supply
masteryZone.sol: Gama bombarded Calicut, captured merchant ships, and cut off the ears and hands of captured sailors to terrify the Zamorin.

masteryZone.q: Where did Vasco da Gama establish the first permanent Portuguese factory (trading post) in India during his second expedition?
masteryZone.sol: He established the first factory at Cochin in 1503 (completed after his arrival/alliance), which became their first headquarters.

masteryZone.q: What were the primary mandates given to Vasco da Gama for his second voyage in 1502? (Select all that apply)
opts: To avenge the massacre of Portuguese factors left by Cabral
To enforce the crown monopoly over the spice trade
To establish trading factories at Cochin and Cannur
To capture Goa and make it the capital of Portuguese India
masteryZone.sol: Gama's 1502 mission was to punish Calicut (avenging the factory massacre), enforce the monopoly, and set up posts at Cochin and Cannur. Goa was captured later in 1510.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following ports became key nodes in the early Portuguese trade network established during the second voyage? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Cochin, Kannur, and Quilon were all early trading partners and factory locations for the Portuguese. Madras was British.

masteryZone.q: Identify the extreme measures taken by Vasco da Gama to terrorize Calicut merchants in 1502. (Select all that apply)
opts: Plundering and burning the Pilgrim ship Miri with passengers on board
Bombarding Calicut port and destroying harbor structures
Mutilating captured crew members and sending them to the Zamorin
Bribing the Zamorin's chief priest to assassinate him
masteryZone.sol: Gama committed brutal acts, including burning the Miri (killing hundreds), bombarding Calicut, and mutilating captives.

masteryZone.q: What benefits did the Raja of Cochin gain from allying with the Portuguese? (Select all that apply)
opts: Military protection against the expansionist Zamorin of Calicut
Access to modern European firearms and naval support
Enhanced trade revenue through the Portuguese factory
Direct annexation of the Vijayanagara territories
masteryZone.sol: Cochin was a vassal of Calicut. Allying with the Portuguese gave them independence and defense against the Zamorin.

masteryZone.q: Which ship types were part of Vasco da Gama's 1502 armed armada? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The fleet consisted of carracks (naus) and caravels equipped with heavy artillery. Steamships did not exist.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Pedro Álvares Cabral's factors in Calicut were massacred by local riots before Gama's second voyage.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, a conflict between Cabral's men and Muslim merchants led to a riot where the Portuguese factory was destroyed and factors killed.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama demanded that the Zamorin expel all Muslim merchants from Calicut as a condition for peace in 1502.
masteryZone.sol: Gama demanded the complete expulsion of all Arab/Muslim traders, which the Zamorin refused.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Raja of Cochin was a close relative and loyal vassal of the Zamorin of Calicut.
masteryZone.sol: He was a bitter rival who resented Calicut's domination and eagerly allied with the Portuguese.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama established the Cartaz system during his first voyage in 1498.
masteryZone.sol: The Cartaz (shipping license) system was developed during and after the second voyage in 1502 to enforce control.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The pilgrim ship Miri was carrying passengers returning from Mecca when Vasco da Gama captured and burned it.
masteryZone.sol: Yes, this was one of the most controversial and brutal incidents of Gama's career, killing over 300 pilgrims.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama captured Goa in 1502 and established the Estado da Índia capital there.
masteryZone.sol: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510. During 1502, Cochin was the primary Portuguese base.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Kolathiri Raja of Kannur refused to allow the Portuguese to establish a factory in his territory.
masteryZone.sol: The Kolathiri welcomed them and allowed a factory at Kannur to counter Calicut.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama returned to Portugal in 1503 with a massive cargo of spices and left a permanent naval patrol.
masteryZone.sol: He left behind a coastal patrol fleet under Vicente Sodré to protect Cochin and blockade Calicut.

masteryZone.q: The commander of the 1500 CE Portuguese voyage was Pedro Álvares __________.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: Vasco da Gama returned in 1502 with a fleet of __________ ships.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: The Portuguese established their first factory at the port of __________.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: Gama captured and burned the pilgrim vessel named __________.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: The ruler of Cochin welcomed the Portuguese to counter the power of the __________ of Calicut.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: The Portuguese naval patrol left behind in 1503 was commanded by Vicente __________.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: Gama demanded the complete expulsion of all __________ merchants from Calicut.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: The first Portuguese fortress built in India (1503) was Fort Emmanuel in __________.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key details of the militarized second voyage.

masteryZone.q: Match the Portuguese expeditions with their years:
masteryZone.sol: Gama's first was 1497-99, Cabral's was 1500-01, and Gama's second was 1502-03.

masteryZone.q: Match the Indian ports with their Portuguese status in 1503:
masteryZone.sol: Cochin was the main ally, Kannur had a secondary factory, and Calicut was blockaded.

masteryZone.q: Match the historical actions of the second voyage with their targets:

options.text: Blockade of the Red Sea route

masteryZone.sol: Miri was the pilgrim ship, Sodré blockaded the Red Sea, and Fort Emmanuel defended Cochin.

masteryZone.q: Why did Gama return to India with a large military fleet in 1502?
masteryZone.sol: To enforce the spice monopoly by force and avenge the massacre of Portuguese factors.

masteryZone.q: Which European nation pioneered the use of ship-borne cannons in the Indian Ocean?
masteryZone.sol: Portugal.

masteryZone.q: Who was the leader of the Cochin alliance that supported Gama?
masteryZone.sol: The Raja of Cochin (Unni Goda Varma).

masteryZone.q: What was the name of the pilgrim ship destroyed by Gama in 1502?
masteryZone.sol: The Miri.

masteryZone.q: Where was the first Portuguese fortress built in India?
masteryZone.sol: Cochin (Fort Emmanuel).

masteryZone.q: What was the main purpose of the Cartaz system introduced during the second voyage?
masteryZone.sol: To force all merchant ships to pay taxes and obtain license from the Portuguese.

masteryZone.q: Why was Vicente Sodré's patrol left in Indian waters?
masteryZone.sol: To protect the Cochin factory and blockade Muslim trade routes.

masteryZone.q: What terms did Gama demand from the Zamorin for peace in 1502?
masteryZone.sol: The expulsion of all Muslim merchants and exclusive trading rights.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama bombarded Calicut and mutilated prisoners during his second voyage.
Reason: He wanted to establish absolute naval terror to break the Zamorin's resistance to the spice monopoly.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The extreme violence was part of a calculated strategy of gunboat diplomacy.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Portuguese established their main base in Cochin rather than Calicut.
Reason: The Raja of Cochin was a rival of the Zamorin and offered land and support to the Portuguese.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The political fragmentation of the Malabar Coast allowed the Portuguese to exploit rivalries.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Pedro Álvares Cabral succeeded in maintaining peace in Calicut.
Reason: He reached an agreement with the Arab merchants to share spice exports.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Cabral's voyage ended in conflict, and his factors were massacred, leading to Gama's retaliatory mission.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The burning of the ship Miri caused outrage across the Indian Ocean.
Reason: The ship was unarmed and carried over 300 civilian pilgrims, including women and children.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The destruction of the Miri was seen as a brutal act of piracy even by Portuguese contemporary standards.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The Cartaz system was accepted voluntarily by all Indian Ocean merchants.
Reason: It guaranteed protection against pirates without any cost or restrictions.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The Cartaz was an enforced license system that forced merchants to pay protection money or face capture.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Gama left a permanent naval force in India in 1503.
Reason: The Portuguese realized that a seasonal presence was insufficient to enforce their monopoly against Arab merchant networks.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Leaving Sodré's patrol was the beginning of permanent European naval presence in Asia.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Fort Emmanuel was constructed in Cochin in 1503.
Reason: It was built to protect the Portuguese factory from attacks by the Zamorin's forces.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The fort was crucial in defending the Cochin factory during subsequent wars with Calicut.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama was appointed Governor-General of India in 1502.
Reason: He successfully defeated the Zamorin's navy at the Battle of Cochin.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Gama was not appointed Governor-General or Viceroy in 1502. Almeida was the first Viceroy in 1505.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Voyage of Vasco da Gama:
1. The fleet consisted of 20 ships, divided into three squadrons.
2. The expedition was funded partly by private merchant syndicates in Lisbon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The 1502 fleet was highly organized and combined royal ships with private merchant backing.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the Cochin alliance, consider these statements:
1. Cochin was Cochin's attempt to liberate itself from Calicut's political dominance.
2. The Portuguese built Fort Emmanuel using stone shipped directly from Lisbon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Cochin sought independence from Calicut. The fort was built using local materials (mainly coconut trunks and earth).

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the pilgrim ship Miri:
1. The ship belonged to the Sultan of Egypt.
2. Gama plundered the ship's cargo before setting it on fire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The Miri belonged to a rich Calicut merchant, though it carried pilgrims. Gama plundered it before burning it.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to early Portuguese factories, consider these statements:
1. A factory was a manufacturing unit producing gunpowder.
2. A factor (feitor) was a royal commercial agent responsible for buying spices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Factories were trading posts (warehouses), not manufacturing units. Factors managed purchase and storage.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Portuguese patrol under Vicente Sodré sailed to the Red Sea but abandoned Cochin.
2. The Zamorin occupied Cochin in 1503 after the patrol left.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Sodré sailed to the Red Sea to plunder, leaving Cochin vulnerable. The Zamorin invaded Cochin, forcing the Raja to flee.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Portuguese factory in Calicut get destroyed in 1500 CE?
masteryZone.sol: Pedro Álvares Cabral seized an Arab merchant vessel. In retaliation, Muslim merchants and local riots attacked and burned the Portuguese factory, killing the factor Aires Correia.

masteryZone.q: Why did Gama demand the expulsion of all Muslims from Calicut during his second voyage?
masteryZone.sol: Gama wanted to eliminate his commercial rivals and establish a complete monopoly for the Portuguese crown. He also blamed them for the 1500 CE massacre.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Raja of Cochin continue his alliance with the Portuguese despite the Zamorin's invasions?
masteryZone.sol: The Raja of Cochin was a vassal of Calicut and sought independence. Breaking the alliance would mean surrender to the Zamorin, who wanted to depose him.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama use naval artillery to change the nature of Indian Ocean warfare in 1502?
masteryZone.sol: Traditional trade ships were unarmed. Gama used heavily armed carracks with cannons to destroy Calicut's fleet from a distance, initiating naval gun warfare.

masteryZone.q: How did the Cartaz system work to enforce the Portuguese trade monopoly?
masteryZone.sol: Every merchant vessel was required to buy a Cartaz (license) from a Portuguese factory, pay customs duties, and agree not to carry prohibited items (like spices or weapons). Ships without it were captured.

masteryZone.q: How did the Portuguese secure their factories physically against land attacks?
masteryZone.sol: They constructed fortified warehouses with stone walls, bastions, and artillery, which evolved into military fortresses like Fort Emmanuel.

masteryZone.q: Analyze the Battle of Calicut (1502) as a study in early modern gunboat diplomacy.
masteryZone.sol: It showed that superior naval artillery could force local rulers to yield or suffer massive economic destruction, redefining diplomacy in Asia.

masteryZone.q: Examine the destruction of the ship Miri as a case study of religious and economic warfare.
masteryZone.sol: Gama's actions against the Miri combined commercial warfare (seizing competitor goods) with crusading zeal (destroying Islamic pilgrim shipping), worsening conflicts.

masteryZone.q: Evaluate the role of the Sodré patrol in establishing the Portuguese naval blockade.
masteryZone.sol: The patrol blockaded the mouth of the Red Sea to stop spice shipments to Egypt, forcing trade to redirect through the Portuguese Cape Route.

masteryZone.q: Explain the function of a 'factory' (feitoria) in the Portuguese commercial system.
masteryZone.sol: It was a fortified trading post and warehouse where factors bought spices from local brokers and stored them until the annual Portuguese fleet arrived.

masteryZone.q: Describe the geopolitical rivalry between Calicut and Cochin and how the Portuguese exploited it.
masteryZone.sol: Cochin was economically and politically subordinate to Calicut. The Portuguese offered Cochin military protection in exchange for exclusive trade, dividing local rulers.

masteryZone.q: Explain the strategic purpose of Fort Emmanuel in Kochi.
masteryZone.sol: It was the first European fort in India, securing the Portuguese presence in Cochin against land invasions by the Zamorin's superior forces.

sections.title: 4. The Third Voyage & Viceroyalty (1524)
sections.content:
Gama's final mission was political rather than commercial:

Curbing Corruption
  • Appointment: Appointed Viceroy in 1524 by King John III to restore order and clean up corruption in the Estado da Índia administration.
  • Death: Contracted malaria shortly after arriving in Kochi and died on Christmas Eve, 1524. He was buried in St. Francis Church, Kochi, before his remains were returned to Portugal in 1539.

masteryZone.q: In which year did Vasco da Gama return to India for his third and final voyage?
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama was sent back to India in 1524 CE by King John III.

masteryZone.q: What official title was bestowed upon Vasco da Gama for his third voyage to India in 1524 CE?
masteryZone.sol: He was appointed the second Viceroy of India (following Francisco de Almeida and Albuquerque, who were Governors/Viceroys).

masteryZone.q: Who was the Portuguese King who appointed Vasco da Gama as Viceroy in 1524 CE?
masteryZone.sol: King John III succeeded King Manuel I and appointed Gama to clean up the corrupt administration.

masteryZone.q: What was the primary administrative objective of Vasco da Gama's final mission to India?
opts: To curb rampant corruption among Portuguese officials
To conquer the Kingdom of Vijayanagara
To shift the capital from Goa to Cochin
To convert the Zamorin to Christianity
masteryZone.sol: The Portuguese administration in India had become highly corrupt. Gama was sent as a strict disciplinarian to restore order.

masteryZone.q: Where in India did Vasco da Gama die on Christmas Eve, 1524 CE?
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama contracted malaria and died in Cochin on December 24, 1524.

masteryZone.q: What problems did Vasco da Gama face when he arrived in India as Viceroy in 1524? (Select all that apply)
opts: Rampant corruption and embezzlement by Portuguese officials
Insubordination and lack of discipline in the military
Declining royal revenues due to illegal private trading
A massive invasion by the Mughal Emperor Babur
masteryZone.sol: Gama faced administrative decay, embezzlement, and private trade by officials. Babur's invasion was in North India and did not affect them.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are true regarding Vasco da Gama's death and burial? (Select all that apply)
opts: He died of malaria in Cochin on Christmas Eve, 1524
He was initially buried in St. Francis Church in Cochin
His remains were exhumed and returned to Portugal in 1539
He was buried in the Basilica of Bom Jesus in Goa
masteryZone.sol: Gama died of malaria, was buried at St. Francis Church in Kochi, and his remains were later moved to Portugal. Bom Jesus holds St. Francis Xavier.

masteryZone.q: What reforms did Vasco da Gama attempt to implement during his brief viceroyalty? (Select all that apply)
opts: Replacing corrupt officials with loyal administrators
Strict auditing of factory accounts and spice storage
Enforcing prohibitions on illegal private trade by soldiers
Abolishing the Cartaz system to encourage free trade
masteryZone.sol: Gama focused on audits, replacing corrupt staff, and banning private trade. He kept the Cartaz system.

masteryZone.q: Identify the key Portuguese governors of India who ruled between Vasco da Gama's second and third voyages. (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Almeida (1505-09), Albuquerque (1509-15), and Albergaria (1515-18) ruled before Gama's return in 1524. Nino da Cunha ruled later (1529-38).

masteryZone.q: Which locations in India have monuments or historical sites directly associated with Vasco da Gama's life or death? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Kappad (landing), St. Francis (burial), and Vasco town (named after him) are directly associated with him.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama was the first official Viceroy of Portuguese India.
masteryZone.sol: Francisco de Almeida was the first Viceroy in 1505. Gama was the second Viceroy, appointed in 1524.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama died of wounds sustained in a battle against the Zamorin's navy.
masteryZone.sol: He died of malaria (or illness) in Cochin, not from battle wounds.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama's remains are currently located in the Jerónimos Monastery in Lisbon.
masteryZone.sol: His body was returned to Portugal in 1539 and eventually interred in the Jerónimos Monastery.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Gama served as Viceroy of India for over ten years before returning to Portugal.
masteryZone.sol: He served for only three months in 1524 before his sudden death.

masteryZone.q: True or False: King John III sent Gama because of his reputation for being harsh and unyielding.
masteryZone.sol: Gama's stern reputation was seen as necessary to control the corrupt Portuguese factions in India.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The St. Francis Church in Kochi where Gama was buried is the oldest European church in India.
masteryZone.sol: Built by the Portuguese in 1503, St. Francis Church is indeed the oldest European-built church in India.

masteryZone.sol: The capital remained in Goa (which was made capital by Albuquerque). Gama only died in Cochin during an administrative tour.

masteryZone.sol: Landed at Kappad, died in Cochin, and rests in Lisbon's Jerónimos Monastery.

masteryZone.sol: John II planned the route, Manuel I sponsored 1st and 2nd voyages, and John III appointed Gama Viceroy.

masteryZone.q: Why did King John III choose Vasco da Gama to return to India in 1524?
masteryZone.sol: Why did King John III choose Vasco da Gama to return to India in 1524?

masteryZone.sol: He contracted malaria shortly after his arrival.

masteryZone.q: Where was Vasco da Gama buried before his remains were taken to Lisbon?
masteryZone.sol: St. Francis Church, Fort Kochi.

What famous monastery in Lisbon houses Vasco da Gama's tomb today?
masteryZone.sol: Jerónimos Monastery.

masteryZone.sol: Embezzlement and illegal private trading by Portuguese officers.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: King John III sent Vasco da Gama back to India in 1524 CE.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Gama's mission was to restore discipline and secure royal revenues from corrupt officials.

masteryZone.q:

Reason: He died in Cochin shortly after arriving in India, before he could settle in Goa.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: His sudden death in Cochin cut short his administrative tour of the settlements.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: St. Francis Church in Kochi was built by the British.
Reason: The British controlled Cochin since 1503 CE and constructed the church to honor Vasco da Gama.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

masteryZone.sol: The church was built by the Portuguese in 1503. The British only took control of Cochin much later.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama's final voyage had a commercial rather than administrative purpose.
Reason: He was sent to establish new factories in Bengal and Gujarat.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: The 1524 mission was purely political and administrative, aimed at reform and anti-corruption.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama was buried with royal honors in Portugal in 1539.
Reason: His remains were exhumed and transported from Cochin back to Lisbon.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

masteryZone.sol: The return of his remains was a major state event to honor the discoverer of the route.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Gama suspended Duarte de Menezes upon his arrival in India.
Reason: Menezes was accused of embezzling royal spice revenues and abusing his gubernatorial authority.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Gama acted decisively to arrest and replace corrupt officials immediately.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: Vasco da Gama was the first European explorer to die in India.
Reason: Francisco de Almeida and Afonso de Albuquerque both died in Portugal after retirement.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Albuquerque died in Goa in 1515, and Almeida died in South Africa in 1510. Gama was not the first.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion: The town of Vasco da Gama in Goa was established during his lifetime.
Reason: He conquered Goa from the Adil Shahi Sultan in 1524 CE.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

masteryZone.sol: The town was named after him much later. Goa was conquered by Albuquerque in 1510, not Gama.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Vasco da Gama's third voyage:
1. He arrived with a fleet of 14 ships and extensive administrative powers.
2. He died in India within three months of landing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are historically accurate. He arrived in Sept 1524 and died in Dec 1524.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to Vasco da Gama's burial, consider these statements:
1. His gravestone can still be seen inside St. Francis Church in Kochi.
2. His actual remains were moved to Portugal in 1539.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The empty tomb and gravestone remain a visitor site in Kochi, while the bones are in Lisbon.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vasco da Gama was succeeded as Viceroy by Afonso de Albuquerque.
2. Gama's reforms successfully eliminated corruption in Portuguese India forever.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Albuquerque died in 1515, long before 1524. Corruption returned quickly after Gama's sudden death.

masteryZone.q:
With reference to the Portuguese administration in 1524, consider these statements:
1. The headquarters of the Estado da India was situated at Goa.
2. Vasco da Gama's administrative jurisdiction extended to Portuguese trade posts in Malacca.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: The capital was Goa, and the Viceroy controlled the entire commercial network from East Africa to Malacca.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding King John III:
1. He was the son of King Manuel I.
2. He reversed the monopolistic trade policies of his predecessor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: He was Manuel's son, but he maintained and intensified the royal monopoly, sending Gama to enforce it.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Portuguese administration in India corrupt by 1524?
masteryZone.sol: Because distance from Lisbon allowed officials to engage in illegal private trade, embezzle crown funds, and abuse their power for personal enrichment.

masteryZone.q: Why did King John III choose Vasco da Gama for the viceroyalty over younger candidates?
masteryZone.sol: Because Gama was a national hero with a fearsome reputation for discipline, loyalty to the crown, and ruthlessness, making him ideal for cleaning up the administration.

masteryZone.q: Why did Cochin remain a key location for Gama's final days instead of Goa?
masteryZone.sol: Cochin was the primary port of arrival and a key center of spice collection. Gama fell ill shortly after arriving in Kochi and died before visiting Goa.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama deal with Governor Duarte de Menezes in 1524?
masteryZone.sol: He immediately suspended and arrested Menezes on charges of corruption, ordering him to be sent back to Portugal under arrest.

masteryZone.q: How did Vasco da Gama's death impact the administrative reforms he had started?
masteryZone.sol: His reforms were cut short. After his death, corrupt practices and private trading slowly returned among the Portuguese officials.

masteryZone.q: How was Vasco da Gama's memory preserved in both India and Portugal after his death?
masteryZone.sol: In India, his empty tomb remains in Kochi, and a town in Goa is named after him. In Portugal, he is interred in Jerónimos Monastery alongside kings.

masteryZone.q: Examine the St. Francis Church in Kochi as a monument of Indo-Portuguese history.
masteryZone.sol: Built in 1503, it is the oldest European church in India. It holds the gravestone of Vasco da Gama, marking the site of his original burial.

masteryZone.q: Analyze the role of the Portuguese Viceroyalty as a administrative system under the Crown.
masteryZone.sol: The Viceroy was a direct representative of the King, holding supreme civil and military authority over all Portuguese territories in Asia.

masteryZone.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of Vasco da Gama's anti-corruption measures.
masteryZone.sol: They were highly effective in the short term due to his uncompromising nature, but failed to survive his sudden death due to systemic corruption.

masteryZone.q: Explain the administrative differences between a Governor and a Viceroy in Portuguese India.
masteryZone.sol: A Viceroy was a royal representative of noble blood, while a Governor was a high official with similar powers but less court prestige.

masteryZone.q: Describe the geographic scale of the Estado da Índia in 1524.
masteryZone.sol: It was a maritime empire stretching from Sofala and Ormuz in the west, to Goa and Cochin in India, and Malacca in the east.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of the exhumation of Gama's remains in 1539.
masteryZone.sol: It marked the recognition of Vasco da Gama's legacy by the crown, bringing his remains to Lisbon as a national symbol of the Age of Discovery.

sections.title: 5. Geopolitical Impact of Gama's Discoveries
sections.content:
Gama's voyages restructured global geopolitics and commerce:

World Trade Realignment
  • Mediterranean Decline: Shifted the center of wealth from Mediterranean city-states (Venice, Genoa) to Atlantic kingdoms (Lisbon, Seville).
  • Colonial Prelude: Set the precedent for armed mercantilism and European colonial extraction in Asia.

masteryZone.q: Which ocean did Vasco da Gama's voyages effectively open to European armed commercial navigation?
masteryZone.sol: Vasco da Gama's voyage opened the Indian Ocean, shifting global maritime trade patterns.

masteryZone.q: The discovery of the Cape Route led to the rapid commercial decline of which European city-state?
masteryZone.sol: Venice had a monopoly on Levant spice trade; the Portuguese Cape Route bypassed it, causing Venetian decline.

masteryZone.q: What term is used for the Portuguese royal shipping fleet system that traveled between Lisbon and Goa?
masteryZone.sol: The 'Carreira da Índia' (Run to India) was the annual line of fleets organized by the Portuguese crown.

masteryZone.q: How did the Portuguese crown manage the spice trade imports in Lisbon?
opts: Through the state department Casa da Índia
By selling trade rights to the British
By allowing open free market trading
masteryZone.sol: Casa da Índia (House of India) was the crown organization that managed all import monopolies and duties.

masteryZone.q: Which empire's revenues were severely impacted by the Portuguese diversion of spice trade from the Red Sea?
masteryZone.sol: The Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt relied on transit taxes on spices. The loss of trade led to their decline and eventual Ottoman conquest.

masteryZone.q: What were the primary geopolitical consequences of Vasco da Gama's maritime breakthrough? (Select all that apply)
opts: The shift of trade supremacy from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic
The decline of Venice and Mamluk Egypt's spice monopolies
The introduction of militarized mercantilism in the Indian Ocean
The immediate collapse of the Chinese Ming dynasty
masteryZone.sol: Gama's route shifted trade to the Atlantic, hurt Venice/Egypt, and brought naval mercantilism. Ming China was unaffected.

masteryZone.q: Which trade centers suffered economic losses due to the rise of the Portuguese Cape Route? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Alexandria, Venice, and Genoa lost their monopoly on spices. Lisbon, conversely, became extremely wealthy.

masteryZone.q: How did the Portuguese enforce their commercial monopoly in the Indian Ocean? (Select all that apply)
opts: By seizing strategic choke points like Malacca and Ormuz
By enforcing the Cartaz licensing system on all local ships
By destroying competitive merchant shipping through naval warfare
By signing free-trade agreements with all local kingdoms
masteryZone.sol: Monopoly was enforced through choke points, the Cartaz system, and naval gun warfare, not free-trade agreements.

masteryZone.q: Identify the key components of the Portuguese 'Estado da Índia' commercial structure. (Select all that apply)
opts: The Casa da Índia in Lisbon
A network of fortified coastal factories (feitorias)
The annual Carreira da Índia fleets
The joint-stock ownership structure of the Dutch model
masteryZone.sol: The Estado da India was a crown monopoly system (Casa, factories, fleets), unlike the later joint-stock Dutch and British companies.

masteryZone.q: What long-term historical processes were initiated by Vasco da Gama's landing in India? (Select all that apply)
opts: Direct European colonial expansion in Asia
Global integration of oceanic trade networks
The spread of Western Christianity in coastal India
The instant destruction of the Silk Road land routes
masteryZone.sol: Landing initiated colonialism, global trade, and Christian missions. Silk Road routes declined but did not disappear instantly.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The shift of global commerce from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic is called the Commercial Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: The opening of ocean routes and expansion of trade is a core part of the Commercial Revolution.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Venice retained its status as the chief spice supplier of Europe throughout the 16th century.
masteryZone.sol: Lisbon replaced Venice as the primary distributor of spices in Western Europe.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Portuguese empire in Asia was based on vast land conquests and inland colonization.
masteryZone.sol: It was a thalassocracy (maritime empire) based on controlling sea lanes, ports, and choke points.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Casa da Índia was a private joint-stock corporation owned by Dutch merchants.
masteryZone.sol: It was a Portuguese crown institution that managed the royal spice trade.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Vasco da Gama's route made Lisbon the richest city in Europe during the early 16th century.
masteryZone.sol: The spice monopoly brought immense wealth directly to the Portuguese crown in Lisbon.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt allied with the Ottoman Empire to fight the Portuguese navy.
masteryZone.sol: The Mamluks fought the Portuguese (e.g. Battle of Diu) but were actually conquered by the Ottomans in 1517.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The discovery of the sea route directly linked Europe to the spices of the Moluccas.
masteryZone.sol: Opening the route to India led directly to Portuguese expansion into Malacca and the Spice Islands (Moluccas).

masteryZone.q: True or False: The Silk Road land trade route was completely closed by the Chinese because of the Portuguese sea route.
masteryZone.sol: The land route became less competitive but remained active; it was not closed by China.

masteryZone.q: The transition of trade centers from Mediterranean to Atlantic ports is part of the __________ Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.q: The Mamluk Sultanate of __________ was devastated by the loss of spice transit taxes.
masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.

masteryZone.sol: Identifies key terms related to the geopolitical impact.
